segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said these things; then, lifting his eyes to heaven, he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son, so that the Son may glorify you,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: just as you gave him authority over all flesh, so that he may give eternal life to all those you have given him.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And this is eternal life: that they know you, the only true God, and the one you sent, Jesus Christ.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I glorified you on earth by finishing the work you gave me to do.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And now, Father, glorify me in your own presence with the glory I had with you before the world existed.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I revealed your name to the people you gave me out of the world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Now they know that everything you have given me is from you,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: for the words you gave me I have given to them, and they received them and truly came to know that I came from you, and they believed that you sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am asking on their behalf. I am not asking on behalf of the world but on behalf of those you have given me, because they are yours,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and all that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine, and I have been glorified in them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am no longer in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name, which you have given me, so that they may be one just as we are.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: While I was with them, I kept them in your name, which you have given me. I guarded them, and not one of them was lost except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But now I am coming to you, and I say these things in the world so that they may have my joy made full in themselves.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I have given them your word, and the world has hated them, because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am not asking that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from the evil one.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Consecrate them in the truth; your word is truth.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Just as you sent me into the world, I also have sent them into the world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And for their sake I consecrate myself, so that they too may be consecrated in truth.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am not asking on behalf of these only, but also on behalf of those who believe in me through their word,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: that they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me and I in you, that they also may be in us, so that the world may believe that you sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The glory that you have given me I have given to them, so that they may be one just as we are one,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I in them and you in me, so that they may be made completely one, so that the world may know that you sent me and loved them just as you loved me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Father, those you have given me—I want them also to be with me where I am, so that they may see my glory, which you have given me because you loved me before the foundation of the world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Righteous Father, the world has not known you, but I have known you, and these have come to know that you sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I made your name known to them, and I will make it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.”

notes.note: “All flesh” is a Semitic idiom, familiar from the Greek Old Testament, for all humanity seen as mortal creatures. Some translations paraphrase it as “all people”; the idiom is kept here because the Greek has it.

The adjective comes from the word for “age,” and in Jewish usage “eternal life” is the life of the age to come, a matter of kind as well as length. That fits verse 3, which defines it as knowing God, not as endless duration. “Eternal” is the standard rendering; a minority of translators render “life of the age to come.”

In biblical usage a person’s name stands for the person as made known: their identity, character and authority. To reveal God’s name is to make God himself known, and to be kept “in your name” (verses 11–12) is to be kept within what that name stands for.

notes.traditional: those whom thou hast given me
notes.note: The earliest manuscripts read “your name, which you have given me,” here and in verse 12. Many later manuscripts read “those whom you have given me,” making the gift the disciples and not the name; this is the reading behind the King James Version. Most modern editions and translations follow the earlier reading.

“Son of” is a Semitic idiom for someone who belongs to or is destined for a thing; the reference is to Judas. The Greek noun for “destruction” is from the same root as the verb “was lost” just before it, so the phrase echoes it: none was lost but the one who belonged to loss. The Scripture in view is not named; many think of the psalm about the betrayer quoted earlier at John 13:18.

The Greek form can be masculine (“the evil one,” meaning the devil) or neuter (“evil” in general). Most modern translations and commentators choose “the evil one,” in line with the same usage in 1 John, but “keep them from evil” is grammatically possible.

The Greek verb is built on the ordinary word for “holy” (compare “Holy Father” in verse 11) and means to set someone apart as belonging to God. “Sanctify,” the traditional word, now suggests to many readers a process of moral improvement; here the point is dedication to a mission (verse 18) and, in verse 19, Jesus dedicating himself, probably as an offering. “Consecrate” is used in both verses to keep that link, as several modern translations do. The phrase “in the truth” can also be read “by the truth.”

Unlike verse 17, the Greek here has no article, so the phrase may mean “in the truth” (the same truth as in verse 17) or simply “truly, really consecrated.” The rendering leaves both possibilities open; most interpreters think the link with verse 17 is intended.

Many manuscripts read “that they also may be one in us,” and this is the familiar wording of older translations. Several of the earliest witnesses lack “one” here, and the edition translated follows them; the word may have been added by copyists from the first clause of the verse.

candidates.reason: Frequent across John and the letters, where translators vary between “glorify,” “honor” and “praise,” and John’s theme of the cross as glorification depends on a consistent rendering.
Used both for obeying a word or command and for protecting people (both senses occur in this chapter), and translations vary between “keep,” “obey,” “protect” and “guard.”
Traditionally “pray” when Jesus addresses the Father but “ask” elsewhere, and it needs to be kept distinct from αἰτέω throughout John and 1 John.

Recurs in Matthew, Paul, Hebrews, 2 Peter and Revelation with renderings ranging from “perdition” and “destruction” to “ruin” and “waste,” and its link to the verb ἀπόλλυμι (“lose, perish”) should be handled consistently.
In John it shifts between the created universe, humanity, and the human order opposed to God, and a register decision would settle whether “world” is kept for all three senses.
